prompt: Sanne, the category manager, wants to know which categories hold products with messy text keys before the product master is cleaned. These tables may hold errors. A sku is off when it is not in standard form: upper case with no spaces anywhere in it. A category_raw is off when it does not equal the category_name of any category, exactly as stored. Some category_raw values spell the parent category TV & Video in several ways instead of naming a category. Return one row for each category_id with at least one product whose sku or category_raw is off, with three columns in this order: category_id; n_sku_off, its products with an off sku; and n_category_raw_off, its products with an off category_raw. The products with a missing category_id form one row of their own, with a missing category_id. Sort by category_id from low to high, with the missing category_id last.
hints: Next, write the two checks as rules on one product: one for the sku and one for category_raw.
Count the products each rule catches for every category_id with conditional counts, and keep only the products that break at least one rule.
why_this_works: Upper-casing a sku and removing every space gives its standard form, and a category_raw that names no category is off, so each count finds one kind of messy key.
